what: Behind the element lies a pastel blob made of nine points placed around it and joined by a curve — each point lifts ±5% of the radius at its own tempo, then the edge slowly undulates, and when the cursor approaches, that point catches up 90% per second and swells up to 8%. Sending fx:full pushes the points out past the four screen corners in .7s power3.out to become a full-screen background (fx:done), and fx:restore shrinks it back in .8s back-blob (a curve that overshoots slightly, wobbles, and settles)

options.points: Number of dots around the edge, default 9
options.wobble: Wobble — fraction of the radius, default .05 (0 means it stops)
options.cursor: Swell share toward the cursor, default .08 (0 turns it off)
options.seed: Number of seeds that set dot angle and tempo — same value gives the same shape, default 1
options.dur: fx:full duration in seconds, default .7 — can also be passed via event detail.dur

use: — To use it as a transition backdrop el.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("fx:full")) Turn the page on fx:done afterward
note: The back-blob curve uses the original CustomEase path values as is — without CustomEase it falls back to back.out(1.4). When full screen, to avoid clipping, the drawing is moved to a fixed spot at the top of the document (.fx-dbm-dock) and drawn there. The original blob also splits into several drops in the loader, but this part makes just one blob.

from.where: index.html scene slider·loader blob, and the blobs beside paragraphs on about·works·detail.html (original BaseIllustrationSlide dots — setFormFullscreen fullScreenProgress 1 .7s power3.out · restore 0 .8s back-blob, group blob --fr .9~.98)
